title: Rollout API: fine-grained permissions, client helpers, shadow traffic and auto-rollback policy
creator: Isabel Choi
description:
Background: As customers adopt model lifecycle practices (canaries, A/B, shadow), we need API and SDK primitives that make rollouts safe, auditable, and easy to integrate into CI/CD. Current APIs expose traffic-split but lack: (1) explicit RBAC surface for who can start/approve/rollback; (2) standard client helpers for idempotent creation and local sampling; (3) shadow traffic control that isolates costs and privacy; (4) server-driven auto-rollback rules tied to observable metrics.

Goals:
- Define a stable REST + SDK surface for creating/managing rollouts including canary, A/B, and shadow variants.
- Provide client helpers for idempotent create/update and local traffic sampling logic.
- Add fine-grained permissions and audit logging for sensitive actions.
- Implement auto-rollback with configurable triggers and safe defaults.

Success metrics: fewer manual rollbacks by customers, decreased user-facing incidents from bad model updates, +50% reduction in support tickets about accidental rollout changes.

Artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ML/Rollout+API+Design, SDK mockups: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1-rollout-sdk-prototypes, prototype dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/rollouts/canary-overview
api_endpoints:
Proposed endpoints (REST):
- POST /v1/rollouts  -> create rollout (idempotency-key header supported)
- GET /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id} -> rollout details + history
- PATCH /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id} -> update targets/conditions
- POST /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/traffic -> adjust traffic split (canary/A-B)
- POST /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/shadow -> toggle/add shadow target
- POST /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/rollback -> manual rollback (reason required)
- GET /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/events -> timeline + trigger reasons
sdk_helpers:
Planned helpers across JS/Python/Go SDKs:
- client.rollouts.createOrGet(params, { idempotencyKey }) -> ensures safe retries
- client.rollouts.simulateTraffic(rolloutSpec, seed) -> local sampling to validate allocations
- client.rollouts.waitForStable(rolloutId, {timeout, successCriteria}) -> helper polling for CI
- client.rollouts.patchTraffic(rolloutId, delta, {dryRun}) -> support dry-run in SDK
- helpers for telemetry: reporter.attachRolloutContext(req, {role, bucketId})

SDK design notes: keep helper names explicit (createOrGet vs create) to surface idempotency semantics to callers. Provide both sync and streaming progress callbacks.
idempotency_strategy: Server-side idempotency modeled after common Create semantics: client supplies Idempotency-Key header (UUID v4 recommended). Behavior: if a create request with an identical key has already succeeded, server returns the existing rollout with 200 and original rollout_id. Idempotency keys expire after 24 hours. For updates, PATCH supports idempotency to prevent duplicate traffic adjustments; keys for updates should be scoped to rollout_id. Error behavior: conflicting parameters with same key -> 409 + explanatory message. SDKs will surface a helper to generate and cache idempotency keys per CI job.
permissions_mapping:
RBAC mappings (new permissions):
- rollout.create -> allows creating rollouts and shadow targets
- rollout.modify -> modifying rollout config/traffic
- rollout.execute -> applying traffic changes and triggering rollouts
- rollout.rollback -> triggering manual rollback
- rollout.view -> read-only access to rollout details/events
- rollout.audit -> view/stream audit logs for rollouts

Roles: 'engineer' -> rollout.create, rollout.view; 'sre' -> rollout.modify, rollout.execute, rollout.view; 'platform-admin' -> all rollout permissions.
All sensitive actions must emit audit entries with actor, ip, and request id. Integration with existing SSO/SAML and customer-managed RBAC (Private customers) must be validated.
auto_rollback:
Auto-rollback behavior:
- Default triggers: error_rate > 5% absolute increase OR 99th p95 latency worsens by > 30% relative, sustained for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows.
- Quality signal trigger: if evaluation harness reports quality regression > X points on user-provided eval set for 2 windows -> auto-rollback.
- Cooldown: once auto-rollback occurs, the system will prevent the same rollout from being retried for 30 minutes without explicit override.
- Notifications: webhook, email, and console banner. Rollback action includes a machine-readable reason and a link to the console event.
- Safe defaults: for Dedicated/Private customers allow configuring thresholds; hosted customers use platform defaults but can provide override policy in rollout spec.
shadow_traffic_spec:
Shadowing primitives:
- Shadow traffic can be attached to any rollout as a list of shadow targets with percentage and sampling_key.
- Shadow requests are cloned and sent to shadow service asynchronously; they do not affect production quotas & are not billable by default (flagged).
- Sampling keys (user_id, session_id) must be configurable to support deterministic routing and stable shadow pairs.
- Privacy: ability to scrub PII from shadow payloads (transform hooks) before forwarding.
- Observation: shadow responses produce candidate metrics and logs that are only visible to rollout.view + rollout.audit roles and stored in a separate namespace to prevent accidental mixing with production metrics.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards and alerts:
- Canary overview dashboard: traffic split, per-variant latency/Error rate, resource consumption.
- SLO integration: link rollout to a target SLO; display burn rate during rollout.
- Alert rules: auto-rollback trigger alert (severity P0), non-fatal degradations (P2).
- Tracing: rollout_id must be propagated via X-Rollout-ID header for request traces and logs.
- Postmortem hooks: when auto-rollback happens, system generates a synthesized incident summary (metrics snapshot + recent PRs) and posts to a configured channel.
migration_plan:
Phased migration:
1) Beta: expose new endpoints behind feature flag; SDKs provide experimental helpers (Q1).
2) Opt-in: customers can opt-in using header X-Rollout-API: v2 for 6 weeks.
3) Deprecation: announce deprecation of old traffic endpoints; provide migration guide and script (contrib tool in SDKs).
4) Hard cutoff: after 90 days, old endpoint returns 410.

Compatibility: SDKs will maintain compatibility shims; provide code samples for common flows (canary -> promote -> rollback).
Docs: migration guide and interactive console walkthrough will be available in release notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- API endpoints implemented and passing integration tests (create/update/traffic/shadow/rollback).
- SDK helpers available in JS and Python with usage examples.
- Idempotency keys work as specified, <=24h TTL, documented behavior on conflicts.
- RBAC enforcement in control plane; audit entries emitted for create/modify/execute/rollback.
- Auto-rollback triggers fire in staging test harness and rollback completes end-to-end.
- Shadow traffic stored separately and scrub hooks available.
- Migration documentation published and two customers onboarded to beta.
- Security review signed off and privacy checklist completed for shadowing.
open_questions:
- Should idempotency keys be required for all create calls or only recommended? (security/abuse trade-off).
- How do we expose evaluation-quality signals from Redwood Optimize to the rollout engine (pull vs push)?
- Billing model for shadow traffic for Dedicated customers (flag + invoice vs free).
- Scope of rollback: step back one step in traffic plan vs full revert to previous model; offer both.
- Do we allow cross-project rollouts (one rollout referencing multiple models) initially?
implementation_notes:
Engineering tasks:
- Schema: rollout table with spec JSON, current_state, last_applied_traffic, audit pointers. Migration: add rollout_events table.
- API: controller + idempotency middleware, validation for shadow transforms.
- SDK: helper lib for idempotency key generation and local sampling.
- Monitoring: new metrics (rollout_started, rollout_promoted, rollback_triggered_auto/manual, shadow_requests) and dashboards.
- Tests: end-to-end tests in staging including simulated quality regression via synthetic eval harness.
- Ops: rate limit control on traffic adjustment endpoints to avoid noisy loops.
